sections.section_title: Dermatomyositis Overview and the Anti‑SAE1 Subtype
sections.description: Provides background on dermatomyositis pathophysiology with emphasis on the rare anti‑SAE1 antibody phenotype that shaped this case’s presentation.
subtopics: Definition and epidemiology of dermatomyositis
Autoantibody spectrum in inflammatory myopathies
"Anti‑SAE1" specificity and its target protein
SUMO pathway involvement in autoimmune activation
Complement‐mediated microvascular injury signature
Typical cutaneous hallmarks—including heliotrope rash and Gottron papules
Proximal muscle weakness patterns seen in SAE1 DM
Common extramuscular manifestations such as ILD and dysphagia
Malignancy risk stratification associated with SAE1 antibodies
(DM features observed in the patient)

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation Red Flags – Neck Sweffing Masquerading Angioedema
sections.description: Describes how progressive neck edema initially mimicked Ludwig’s angina or iatrogenic angioedema despite underlying dermatomyositis.
subtopics: Three‐week history of progressive cervical soft tissue swelling
Differentiating Ludwig’s angina versus histamine/bradykinin edema
"Pocket” weakness noted at hip flexors prior to overt facial rash
"Non-tender" erythema over nasolabial folds raised suspicion against allergic etiology
"Subtle nailfold changes" revealing periungual erythema
"Limited purpura" absent rules out urticarial vasculitis
"Normal respiratory rate" arguing against sepsis
"Absence of medication triggers" discount ACEI/-DPP4‐related angioedema

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Work‑up – From Routine Labs to Confirmation Biopsy
sections.description: Lays out the logical sequence from basic laboratory screening through advanced serologies, imaging studies and histopathology culminating in definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: "CBC / CRP" trend revealing mild inflammation without leukocytosis
"Serum muscle enzymes" annotation—CK >16 000 U/L signifying extensive necrosis
"ANA speckled titers" confirming systemic autoimmune state
"Euroimmun myositis panel" strong anti‑SAE1 signal confirmatory antibody profile
"Complement levels" reassuring against hereditary angioedema
"Capillaroscopy" demonstrating nailfold telangiectasia characteristic of DM
"CT neck" documenting diffuse strap muscle edema extending abnormally

"Chest CT" revealing basal ground glass attributable mainly to aspiration 
 and excluding pulmonary fibrosis
"MRI thighs" highlighting perifascicular edema in obturator/internal muscles
"FDG-PET" confirming widespread muscle inflammation without focal malignancy
"Muscle biopsy" showing vacuolated necrotic fibers + C5b9 deposition characteristic
